title: Implement gesture-based animations (swipe to dismiss, pull-to-refresh)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Mobile users expect gesture-based interactions. Currently panels only dismiss via close button, and there's no pull-to-refresh.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Implement swipe-to-dismiss for panels (swipe down on mobile)
2. Implement pull-to-refresh for lists (inventory, collection, quests)
3. Add swipe gestures for navigation (swipe between panels)
4. Ensure gestures have visual feedback (rubber band effect, progress indicator)

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
-- Swipe to dismiss
local function enableSwipeToDismiss(panel)
  local startY = nil
  local currentY = nil
  
  panel.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
    if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
      startY = input.Position.Y
    end
  end)
  
  panel.InputChanged:Connect(function(input)
    if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch and startY then
      currentY = input.Position.Y
      local deltaY = currentY - startY
      if deltaY > 0 then
        -- Rubber band effect
        local progress = math.min(deltaY / 200, 1)
        panel.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, deltaY * 0.5)
        panel.BackgroundTransparency = 0.1 + progress * 0.3
      end
    end
  end)
  
  panel.InputEnded:Connect(function(input)
    if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch and startY and currentY then
      local deltaY = currentY - startY
      if deltaY > 100 then
        -- Dismiss
        hidePanels()
      else
        -- Snap back
        TweenService:Create(panel, TweenInfo.new(0.3), {
          Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0),
          BackgroundTransparency = 0.1
        }):Play()
      end
      startY = nil
      currentY = nil
    end
  end)
end

-- Pull to refresh
local function enablePullToRefresh(scrollFrame, onRefresh)
  -- Similar implementation with progress indicator
end
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- Swipe to dismiss works on all panels
- Pull to refresh works on all lists
- Gestures have visual feedback
- Performance is acceptable on mobile

title: EPIC 31 REVISED: Loading States & Empty States — Zero Blank Screens, Error Handling, Offline Support
EPIC 31: Loading States & Empty States — Eliminate Blank Screens
description:
**BACKGROUND & RATIONALE:**

After the design system foundation (EPIC 30), the next critical issue is that most panels show blank content during network requests. Only the collection panel has a skeleton loader. This creates a broken/unresponsive feel on slow connections.

**CURRENT STATE:**
- Collection panel: ✅ Has skeleton loader (showCollectionSkeleton)
- All other panels: ❌ Show blank content during async loads
- Empty states: ❌ Most panels lack helpful empty states

**WHY THIS MATTERS:**
1. **Perceived performance**: Loading states make the app feel responsive even when data is slow
2. **User confidence**: Users know the app is working, not broken
3. **First impressions**: New users on slow connections see blank screens and leave
4. **Empty states**: Guide users on what to do next when there's no content

**IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:**
1. Create a universal skeleton loader component (reusable across panels)
2. Add loading states to all panels with async data (shop, quests, raid, inventory)
3. Create contextual empty states for each panel
4. Add loading spinners for quick operations (button clicks, toggles)

**DEPENDENCIES:**
- Depends on EPIC 30 (design system) for consistent styling
- Should be done BEFORE EPIC 32 (mobile/accessibility) because loading states affect the core UX

**CONSIDERATIONS:**
- Skeleton loaders should match the final layout (not generic boxes)
- Empty states should be helpful, not just "nothing here"
- Loading spinners should be subtle (don't block the UI)
- Must handle error states (network failures)

**SUCCESS CRITERIA:**
- Zero blank screens during normal operation
- All panels show appropriate loading/empty/error states
- Skeleton loaders match final layout
- Empty states guide users on next actions

title: Create gradient library (surface, accent, status gradients)
description:
**CONTEXT:**
Gradients are used inconsistently. Need a library of reusable gradient presets.

**WHAT TO DO:**
1. Create gradient presets:
   - Surface gradients (subtle background variations)
   - Accent gradients (buttons, highlights)
   - Status gradients (progress bars, health indicators)
   - Rarity gradients (fish rarity colors)
2. Document usage patterns
3. Apply consistently across UI

**IMPLEMENTATION:**
```lua
local GRADIENTS = {
  surface = {
    default = { from = Color3.fromRGB(26, 38, 57), to = UI.surface.primary },
    elevated = { from = Color3.fromRGB(36, 48, 67), to = UI.surface.secondary },
  },
  accent = {
    primary = { from = Color3.fromRGB(56, 152, 255), to = Color3.fromRGB(100, 180, 255) },
    success = { from = Color3.fromRGB(52, 199, 123), to = Color3.fromRGB(100, 220, 160) },
    warning = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 184, 64), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 210, 100) },
    error = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 92, 92), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 140, 140) },
  },
  rarity = {
    Common = { from = Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200), to = Color3.fromRGB(150, 150, 150) },
    Rare = { from = Color3.fromRGB(100, 150, 255), to = Color3.fromRGB(50, 100, 200) },
    Epic = { from = Color3.fromRGB(167, 139, 250), to = Color3.fromRGB(120, 80, 200) },
    Legendary = { from = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 92), to = Color3.fromRGB(255, 160, 50) },
  },
}

local function applyGradient(element, preset)
  local config = GRADIENTS[preset]
  if not config then return end
  local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
  gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new(config.from, config.to)
  gradient.Rotation = 90
  gradient.Parent = element
  return gradient
end
```

**VERIFICATION:**
- All gradient presets render correctly
- Gradients are applied consistently
- Performance is acceptable

EPIC 34: Animation & Motion Design — Micro-interactions, Transitions, Physics
description:
**BACKGROUND & RATIONALE:**

After the design system foundation (EPIC 30) and loading states work (EPIC 31), the next critical issue is that Harbor Heist lacks any motion design. The UI feels static and unpolished, missing modern premium feel that users expect from games like Roblox experiences or mobile apps.

**CURRENT STATE:**
- ❌ No micro-interactions on buttons, toggles, or navigation elements
- ❌ No page transitions between panels (instant, jarring switches)
- ❌ No physics-based animations for objects (fish, items, UI elements)
- ❌ No gesture-based interactions (swipe to dismiss, pull-to-refresh)
- ❌ No easing/physics on any motion — everything is instant or linear

**WHY THIS MATTERS:**
1. **Premium feel**: Motion design separates good apps from great ones (Stripe, Linear, Vercel all have sophisticated animations)
2. **User delight**: Micro-interactions provide instant feedback and make the app feel responsive
3. **Visual hierarchy**: Transitions guide users through the UI flow naturally
4. **Mobile UX**: Gesture-based interactions are essential for mobile-first design

**IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY:**
1. Create a reusable animation system with easing curves (ease-in-out, bounce, elastic)
2. Implement micro-interactions on all interactive elements:
   - Button press animations (scale down on click, ripple effect)
   - Toggle switches with smooth state transitions
   - Navigation hover states with subtle movement
3. Add page transitions between panels:
   - Fade + slide combinations for panel opens/closes
   - Staggered entrance animations for content items
4. Implement physics-based motion:
   - Fish swimming patterns with natural movement
   - Item pickup/drop animations
   - UI elements responding to user actions (drag, throw)
5. Add gesture support:
   - Swipe to dismiss panels/cards
   - Pull-to-refresh on collection list
   - Pinch to zoom on maps/overlays

**DEPENDENCIES:**
- Depends on EPIC 30 (design system) for consistent spacing/sizing tokens
- Should be done BEFORE EPIC 35 (visual polish) because animations enhance the premium feel
- Requires Roblox Animation API familiarity and best practices

**CONSIDERATIONS:**
- Performance: Animations must run at 60fps on mobile devices
- Accessibility: Motion should have reduced-motion alternatives for users who prefer it
- Consistency: All animations follow the same easing curves and timing patterns
- Testing: Must test on low-end devices to ensure smooth performance

**SUCCESS CRITERIA:**
- All interactive elements have micro-interactions (buttons, toggles, navigation)
- Page transitions are smooth with appropriate easing
- Physics-based motion feels natural for game objects
- Gesture interactions work reliably on mobile
- No jank or dropped frames during animations
- Reduced-motion mode respected for accessibility

**SCOPE:**
This epic includes:
1. Animation system foundation (easing, timing, physics)
2. Micro-interactions implementation
3. Page transitions and panel animations
4. Gesture-based interactions
5. Physics-based motion for game objects

**ESTIMATED EFFORT:**
- Phase 1: Animation system + micro-interactions — ~60 minutes
- Phase 2: Transitions + gestures — ~90 minutes  
- Phase 3: Physics motion — ~120 minutes
- Total: ~4.5 hours (can be split across multiple sessions)

**BLOCKING ISSUES:** None
**UNBLOCKED BY:** EPIC 35, harborheist-i39g, harborheist-kboe, harborheist-ks2m

title: Mobile action stack shrinks to 36px on short landscape phones (hqn1 tradeoff)
description: Found during harborheist-rk2h audit: layoutMobileStack clamps scale to 0.6, yielding 36px buttons on ~375px-high landscape phones — below the 44px touch-target minimum. Raising the floor reintroduces the hqn1 bug (QUEST/RAID/BOAT pushed off-screen, unreachable). Needs a design decision (scrollable stack, fewer buttons, or landscape-specific layout), not a clamp tweak. Desktop action bar is also 42px tall (pointer-only, lower priority).
